title: How do we find the area of a trapezium drawn on a grid?
description: A trapezium is drawn on squared paper with a right angle at one corner. A straight line cuts it into a square and a triangle, and their two areas are added. Keeko doubts this and multiplies the top side by the bottom side, which fills a rectangle that is bigger than the shape.
teaching_notes: One idea: a trapezium splits into a square and a triangle, and the area is the sum of the two. Watch for students who multiply the two parallel sides, which gives the rectangle round the shape.

source: Trapezium ABCD on a grid has AB = 4 units, DC = 6 units and height AD = 4 units, with a right angle at D
video_script.why: The child can find areas of squares and triangles, and here meets a trapezium by breaking it into figures whose areas are known.
video_script.substitution: Drop a line from B straight down to DC, find the square and the triangle, and add.
video_script.anchor: the trapezium ABCD of the book drawn on squared paper
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko multiplies the top side four by the bottom side six and says the area is twenty four square units. That is the rectangle round the trapezium, with an empty corner of four square units above the triangle.
video_script.payoff_line: The trapezium covers twenty square units.
maths_rules: trapezium ABCD: AB parallel to DC, AB = 4, DC = 6, AD = 4, right angle at D
drop BM perpendicular to DC: ABMD is a square, 4 x 4 = 16 square units
MC = 6 - 4 = 2; triangle BMC: 1/2 x 2 x 4 = 4 square units
Keeko: 4 x 6 = 24 is the rectangle round the shape; 24 - 20 = 4, the empty corner above triangle BMC
video_script.design: One trapezium on squared paper stays all video. A line splits it into a square and a triangle in two colours, and the sum is built under them. Keeko's rectangle is drawn round the same shape.

narration: <bookmark mark='name'/>A four sided shape with one pair of parallel sides is called a trapezium.
<bookmark mark='drop'/>Name the corners eigh B C D. Drop a line from B straight down to D C, and call the spot M.
<bookmark mark='cut'/>The line cuts the trapezium into a square and a triangle.

<bookmark mark='height'/>The left side eigh D is four units and makes a right angle with D C.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: square ABMD, area = side × side = 4 × 4 = 16 square units

narration: <bookmark mark='sq'/>Step one, find the square. Its area is side times side, because all four sides are four units.
<bookmark mark='sqv'/>Four times four gives sixteen square units.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: MC = 6 - 4 = 2; triangle BMC, area = 1/2 × base × height = 1/2 × 2 × 4 = 4 square units

marks.mc: MC = 6 - 4 = 2 is written on the base of the triangle

narration: <bookmark mark='mc'/>Step two, find the triangle. M C is six take away four, so it is two units.
<bookmark mark='tri'/>Area of a triangle is half times base times height, so half times two times four.
<bookmark mark='tv'/>That gives four square units.

marks.add: the two shaded pieces slide together and the words square + triangle are written

narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step three, add the two areas, because the trapezium is made of the square and the triangle.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Sixteen plus four.

<bookmark mark='ans2'/>That is the area of the shape on the squared paper.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the area is four times six, which is twenty four square units.
<bookmark mark='box'/>But four by six is the rectangle drawn round the whole trapezium.
<bookmark mark='empty'/>That rectangle has an empty corner above the triangle, and the corner is not part of the shape.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The shape is smaller than the rectangle, so we add only the square and the triangle.
